cards.explanation: The answer is to build up the church. Paul says, "All of these must be done to build up the church." Every psalm, teaching and tongue is there for the people in the room. It's like a cookie box: the cookies aren't there to look good, they're there for whoever opens the lid.

The answer is that someone must interpret. Paul says two or at most three should speak in turn, "…and someone must interpret." (1 Corinthians 14:27) Taking turns plus an interpreter is the whole setup, friends. And if there's no interpreter, he says the speaker should remain silent in the church and speak only to himself and God (1 Corinthians 14:28).

The answer is True. Paul says if there is no interpreter, "…he should remain silent in the church…" He isn't told to stop for good, though. He can "…speak only to himself and God." The church part waits for an interpreter.

The answer is True! Paul says, "Two or three prophets should speak, and the others should weigh carefully what is said." So the listeners have a job too, and it isn't just sitting there nodding. Listening with your whole brain counts as work, friends. I can't even listen to my own timer that closely.

The answer is that the first speaker should stop. Paul says, "And if a revelation comes to someone who is seated, the first speaker should stop." The speaker makes room for the new word. Picture me with a stamp mid-press and somebody yelling "hold up!" I'd lift that mustache so fast.

The reason is so everyone may be instructed. Paul says they can all prophesy in turn "…so that everyone may be instructed and encouraged." Turns open the door for everyone to be instructed and encouraged, friends.

The answer is peace. Paul says, "For God is not a God of disorder, but of peace…" That's the reason behind the turns, the interpreter and the stopping. The rules aren't there to squash anybody. They match who God is, friends.

The answer is False. After calling God a God of peace, Paul adds, "…as in all the churches of the saints." So Corinth isn't the only church in view. He points to all the churches. That's a lot of meetings to keep peaceful, friends.

The answer is the law. Paul says women "…must be in submission, as the law says." He names the law, and the verse doesn't point to a specific passage in it. So I'll stay right where the text stays, friends.

The answer is True. Paul says, "If anyone considers himself a prophet or spiritual person, let him acknowledge that what I am writing you is the Lord’s command." He's talking to people who see themselves as spiritual. Those are the very people he asks to acknowledge it, friends.

The answer is that he himself will be ignored. Paul says, "But if anyone ignores this, he himself will be ignored." Hear how the words echo each other, ignores and ignored? Paul stops there. He doesn't say who will do the ignoring or spell out more.

The answer is prophesy. Paul says, "So, my brothers, be eager to prophesy…" After all the rules, he doesn't just say hush. He tells them to be eager. That's a whole lot of excitement for a letter about turns, friends.
The answer is False. Paul says, "…do not forbid speaking in tongues." So the turns and the interpreter don't mean tongues get banned. He tells them not to forbid it, friends.

The answer is a proper and orderly manner, friends. Paul closes with, "But everything must be done in a proper and orderly manner." It's the same thought as God not being a God of disorder (1 Corinthians 14:33). Everything in the meeting gets done that way, and Paul ends on it.
